title: 5 Things I Wish I Knew Before I Started Lifting
summary: Advice to his younger self, inspired by Basement Bodybuilding: follow a program, stay flexible, don't be stubborn, set goals without deadlines, befriend your body, and avoid bad influences from YouTube Fitness. He describes his own mistakes: years stuck in a powerlifting mindset, training through broken bones, and losing his purpose to influencers. Building a strong identity is the core lesson.
claims: Most of what you watch on YouTube should be information that improves your life; 70% entertainment is wasting your life and making others money
A good teacher admits he used to be stupid; every big lifter started small and has simply been at it longer
Early on, experimenting without optimal programming builds instinct, but too much winging it wastes time
A program is a map toward your goal body; training without one is wandering a forest
He trained without a program his first 2 years; the next 3 years on a simple linear program with dumbbells in his bedroom were his best gains, taking him from skinny to visibly trained
The program works for you, not the other way around; modify it when life or plateaus demand
There is no final program because your body keeps evolving; two years earlier he was still pushing the 'final program' idea
'Forever stupidity': every five years you should look back and see you were an idiot, which proves you progressed; there is no finish line
Like a tempered sword, you need discipline and flexibility together or you break at the first obstacle
Handling plateaus by backing off weight then piling it back on is like running into the same wall again with more speed
He was stuck in a powerlifting mindset for years, roughly 2017-2018 to 2021, before properly transitioning to bodybuilding training
Keep an open eye for new methods even when the current one works; stubbornness made him waste years
Have a goal body and a plan, but no deadline: deadlines make you rush and take shortcuts
He enjoyed his early years because the journey mattered; chasing a finish line turned lifting into self-punishment
'Get big in two months' content feeds on your fears, insecurity and impatience
Make friends with your body: bragging about puking, limping or training through tendonitis is short-sighted
His most productive years came when he loved lifting, his worst when he followed 'no pain no gain': he overate and squatted and deadlifted with broken bones
Young men who over-diet toward anorexia to get shredded act from impatience, not love for the body
After he found YouTube Fitness he followed others' plans, his growth stopped and he was constantly in pain
If fitness content hinders you, unsubscribe, including from him, and focus on yourself
If you don't have a goal, others will hand you one that serves them
Choose to be happy now instead of waiting to reach the finish line
The most important thing is to build a strong identity; then you'll build the body you like regardless of others' opinions
